qs.q: When evaluating a child's growth chart over time, which finding on the growth curve is considered the most alarming or dangerous?
qs.e: The direction of the growth curve is more important than its absolute position; a downward curve is considered very dangerous, whereas a horizontal curve is static. A child's curve should ideally remain parallel to the printed reference curves.

qs.q: When interpreting growth charts over time, what pattern indicates the most concerning or 'very dangerous' direction for a child's growth curve?
qs.e: A downward growth curve is classified as very dangerous, while a horizontal curve is considered static. A good curve runs parallel to the printed reference curves on the chart.

qs.q: The new WHO Growth Charts (2006) were developed based on studies in how many countries?
qs.e: The new WHO Growth Charts (2006) were based on studies conducted in six countries. The number 8500 refers to the number of children studied.
